methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Infrastructure cost externalization onto residential ratepayers reveals concentrated AI capability in NoVA data centers creating statewide burdens without distributed benefits—deepening the capability-burden asymmetry that defines Pockets of Excellence.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots capability distribution through peer networks, signaling potential for deep, community-driven AI fluency outside traditional tech hubs if these efforts scale and sustain.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education beyond elite tech corridors, suggesting Richmond could become a secondary node for deep capability development rather than remaining dependent on NoVA spillover.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab targets leadership training rather than broad workforce capability, suggesting institutional AI adoption concentrated in higher education without clear pathways to distributed regional fluency—depth without distribution.

signals.title: AI in Roanoke County schools: How new policies will guide student use - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: School AI policies in Roanoke County focus on regulated student usage of existing platforms rather than building deep AI literacy or development capability, signaling shallow platform-mediated adoption that fits the 'Software Does It For You' pattern.
